relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: structural reference - GUEST appears in the example config specifically to be turned off

cross_product_finding: User creation itself is almost pure identity provisioning (name + password, or an OIDC-federated auto-register) - it carries no privilege or role at creation time by default; access is a wholly separate act performed afterward via the admin_channels/admin_roles properties (see access-control-how-assign-users-to-roles.json). This separation of 'who are you' from 'what can you reach' is sharper in SGW than in server/'s RBAC, where creating a user and granting it privileges are typically the same admin action, and sharper than Capella's model, where a credential (API key or DB credential) is generally minted already scoped to a role. The disabled-by-default GUEST user shown in the example config is also notable: it is the anonymous/unauthenticated identity (referenced elsewhere in this batch's sync-function.json as the implicit actor behind unauthenticated requests, e.g. for public-channel access) and disabling it is presented as a routine security hardening step - a concept with no direct analogue in server/'s or Capella's access-control docs covered so far, since neither exposes an anonymous pseudo-identity as something you provision and then explicitly turn off.
